Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on newly formed
Tropical Storm Dolly, located over the central tropical Atlantic.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&

header WTNT34 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT4.

header WTNT24 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT4.

item.title: Tropical Storm Dolly Public Advisory Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM AST Thu Aug 27 2026 
019 
WTNT34 KNHC 272039
TCPAT4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Dolly Advisory Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL042026
500 PM AST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
...DOLLY MOVING QUICKLY WESTWARD...
...INTERESTS IN THE LEEWARD ISLANDS SHOULD MONITOR...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM AST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...13.7N 40.7W
ABOUT 1425 MI...2290 KM E OF THE LEEWARD ISLANDS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 24 MPH...39 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1007 MB...29.74 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the Leeward Islands should monitor the progress of
Dolly.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM AST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Dolly was
located near latitude 13.7 North, longitude 40.7 West. Dolly is
moving toward the west near 24 mph (39 km/h), and this motion is
expected to continue for the next couple of days.  On the forecast
track, this system should be nearing the Leeward Islands this
weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Little change in strength is likely during the next 48 
hours, and Dolly is forecast to degenerate into a tropical wave 
before it reaches the Leeward Islands.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60 miles (95 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1007 mb (29.74 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Dolly can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT4 and WMO header WTNT44 KNHC.
 
RAINFALL:  Heavy rain from Dolly could affect the Leeward Islands 
late Saturday into Sunday, with rainfall moving into the Virgin 
Islands, Puerto Rico and Hispaniola Sunday and Monday.  This heavy 
rain may produce flash flooding, especially in areas of higher 
terrain of the Leeward Islands.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM AST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Dolly Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM AST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTNT44 KNHC 272040
TCDAT4
 
Tropical Storm Dolly Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL042026
500 PM AST Thu Aug 27 2026

Dolly has been struggling to develop deep thunderstorm activity 
near the center during the day, though a new convective burst has 
recently gone up in the southern semicircle.  Overall the 
environment appears rather dry, with most of the northern portion 
of the circulation exposed.  Satellite Dvorak estimates suggest 
little change in wind speed, so the initial intensity remains 35 kt 
on this advisory.  
 
The initial motion estimate continues at 275/21 kt.  Dolly 
is forecast to move quickly westward for the next couple of days 
under a strong ridge of high pressure over the central Atlantic.  
There aren't many guidance changes to report as the models are 
tightly clustered on a path towards the Leeward Islands.  No 
significant changes were made to the previous NHC forecast, 
remaining on the faster and southward side of the guidance 
envelope.  
 
The environment around Dolly will likely become unfavorable for
strengthening on Friday with increasing southwesterly shear due
to a central Atlantic upper-level trough, fast forward motion and
dry air aloft.  Until then, some modest intensification is
possible, consistent with the model consensus.  Global and regional 
models all show Dolly degenerating into a strong tropical wave on 
Friday or Saturday before it reaches the Leeward Islands, and our 
forecast shows this decay by the weekend.  The timing of the 
transition was moved up slightly from the last advisory, otherwise 
no other changes were made to the forecast.  Post-tropical 
positions are provided at 48-60h given the risk of gusty winds and 
heavy rainfall.
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Heavy rains from Dolly or its remnants could affect the Leeward 
Islands late Saturday into Sunday with possible impacts in the 
Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, and Hispaniola Sunday and Monday.  This 
heavy rain may produce flash flooding, especially in areas of 
higher terrain of the Leeward Islands.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  28/0600Z 14.1N  43.9W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  28/1800Z 14.7N  48.5W   40 KT  45 MPH
 36H  29/0600Z 15.6N  53.1W   40 KT  45 MPH
 48H  29/1800Z 16.5N  57.3W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
 60H  30/0600Z 17.3N  61.5W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROPICAL

$$
Forecaster Blake
